---
title: "Lab 08 — Survival analysis: Kaplan–Meier and Cox regression"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
vet <- read_csv("data/veteran.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    trt = factor(trt, levels = c("standard", "test")),
    celltype = factor(celltype, levels = c("squamous", "smallcell", "adeno", "large")),
    prior = factor(prior, levels = c("no", "yes"))
  )
fit_cox <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ trt + karno + celltype + age, data = vet)
vet_split <- survSplit(Surv(time, status) ~ ., data = vet, cut = c(90, 180),
                       episode = "tgroup", id = "id")
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab08", title = "Survival analysis: Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression",
                 open = c("q9", "q10"))
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Median survival (95% CI) in the standard and test arms is…",
  q2 = "The log-rank test for treatment gives chi-square 0.008 (p = 0.93). The best reading is…",
  q3 = "The exponential MLE of the death rate, with its standard error, is…",
  q4 = "The exponential model and the Kaplan-Meier curve show that…",
  q5 = "In the Cox model trt + karno + celltype + age, the hazard ratio per 10 Karnofsky points is…",
  q6 = "The hazard ratio for adeno vs squamous is 3.25. This means…",
  q7 = "Which statement about cox.zph(fit_cox) is correct?",
  q8 = "With a separate karno coefficient for 0-90, 90-180 and >180 days, the hazard ratio per 10 points in the first 90 days is…",
  q9 = "Why must censored patients be kept in the analysis, and how does Kaplan-Meier use them?",
  q10 = "Interpretation memo (about 150 words): treatment, cell type and Karnofsky score, with estimates and 95% CIs."
)
```

## What you will do

Use the veteran lung cancer trial (`vet`, already loaded). Compute the numbers in the code boxes, then answer. Download the `.txt` at the end.

## Kaplan–Meier and log-rank

```{r km-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=5}
km_trt <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ trt, data = vet)
km_trt
survdiff(Surv(time, status) ~ trt, data = vet)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("103 days (59 to 132) for standard and 52.5 days (44 to 95) for test.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("52.5 days (44 to 95) for standard and 103 days (59 to 132) for test."),
  answer("124 days for standard and 136 days for test."),
  answer("80 days in both arms."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("No evidence that the two survival curves differ; the curves cross, so early and late differences partly cancel.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The test treatment has been shown to be as good as the standard one."),
  answer("The test treatment halves survival, because its median is half as long."),
  answer("The test is invalid because 9 patients are censored."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Exponential model

```{r exp-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
d <- sum(vet$status)
tot <- sum(vet$time)
c(lambda = d / tot, se = d / tot / sqrt(d))
fit_exp <- survreg(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = vet, dist = "exponential")
exp(-coef(fit_exp))
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("0.00768 deaths per person-day, se 0.00068.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.00822 deaths per person-day, se 0.00070."),
  answer("0.00768 deaths per person-day, se 0.0884."),
  answer("130 deaths per person-day, se 11.5."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  answer("The exponential curve lies above Kaplan-Meier in the first months (median 90 vs 80 days) and the Weibull shape 0.85 < 1 points to a hazard that falls with time.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The exponential model fits perfectly because the likelihood ratio test against the Weibull is not significant."),
  answer("The Weibull shape 0.85 < 1 points to a hazard that increases with time."),
  answer("The exponential median, 130 days, equals the Kaplan-Meier median."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Cox regression

```{r cox-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
fit_cox <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ trt + karno + celltype + age, data = vet)
round(cbind(HR = exp(coef(fit_cox)), exp(confint(fit_cox))), 3)
exp(10 * coef(fit_cox)["karno"])
exp(10 * confint(fit_cox)["karno", ])
```

```{r q5}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q5"]],
  answer("0.72 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.80).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.968 (95% CI 0.958 to 0.978)."),
  answer("1.39 (95% CI 1.25 to 1.54)."),
  answer("0.033 (95% CI 0.022 to 0.043)."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q6}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q6"]],
  answer("On average over follow-up, an adeno-carcinoma patient alive at a given time dies at about 3.25 times the rate of a squamous-cell patient with the same treatment, Karnofsky score and age, assuming proportional hazards (only approximate for cell type).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Adeno-carcinoma patients live 3.25 times shorter than squamous-cell patients."),
  answer("The probability of death is 3.25 times higher for adeno-carcinoma patients by the end of the study."),
  answer("Adeno-carcinoma causes 3.25 times as many deaths as squamous-cell cancer in the population."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Proportional hazards

```{r zph-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
cox.zph(fit_cox)
fit_step <- coxph(Surv(tstart, time, status) ~ trt + celltype + age + karno:strata(tgroup),
                  data = vet_split)
round(summary(fit_step)$coefficients, 4)
exp(10 * coef(fit_step)[grep("karno", names(coef(fit_step)))])
```

```{r q7}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q7"]],
  answer("karno (p = 0.0003) and celltype (p = 0.002) show evidence of non-proportional hazards; trt does not.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Only trt violates proportional hazards."),
  answer("The global p-value of 5.6e-05 shows that the Cox model fits well."),
  answer("No covariate violates proportional hazards at the 5% level."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q8}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q8"]],
  answer("0.62, and close to 1 after 90 days: baseline fitness predicts early deaths.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.72 in every period, as in the proportional hazards model."),
  answer("1.07, and 0.62 after 90 days: fitness matters only late."),
  answer("0.95, because the coefficient per point is -0.048."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
